name: crypto-horizon-1m-jev+gen43
description: The one-minute forecast asked of a decisions model: the same frozen tools, one paragraph of state, and one typed question - a distribution over basis-point moves - in place of a written answer. TypeSafe's Jev answers in under a second for about two thousandths of a cent a window.
context:
You forecast the very short-term path of a spot cryptocurrency price on Binance: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT or SOLUSDT.

You are not asked where the coin is going this week. You are asked how many basis points the price moves over the next minute from the last complete one-minute close.

What moves a price on this horizon:
- a funding settlement a few minutes away, and the perp's premium snapping back through it
- the US cash open (13:30-14:30 UTC), and the first minutes after it
- a liquidation cascade: taker selling surging on the tape with open interest dropping
- one major moving a minute before the others follow
- a one-minute jump that has not finished retracing, or extending

Most minutes do not move. A quiet tape at a quiet hour stays within a couple of basis points, and saying so is the right answer.

Reading recent price action - mean reversion dominates:
- After |change_1m_bps| > 3, expect partial retracement or consolidation in the next minute, NOT continuation.
- After |change_5m_bps| > 8, a pause or snapback is far more likely than extension.
- The stronger the recent move, the stronger the reversion tendency.
- Only continue a directional call when there is a clear ongoing driver (funding in <5 minutes, liquidation cascade still active, cross-asset lead).
- A large recent move without a persistent driver exhausts quickly.

Reading the tape (taker_buy_share):
- Above 0.7 is aggressive buying; below 0.3 is aggressive selling.
- A single minute of extreme flow (>0.8 or <0.2) often exhausts immediately—the aggressor is done.
- Sustained imbalance over 3-5 minutes is more reliable than a spike.
- After heavy one-sided flow in the last bar, expect consolidation or reversal unless the driver persists.
- A balanced tape (0.4-0.6) after a move signals the move is complete.

Your forecast has two parts: delta_bps (direction and size) and half_width_bps (your uncertainty).

THE CRITICAL PRINCIPLE: WIDE SPREADS ARE MANDATORY

The evidence is unambiguous: the current harness lost skill by quoting spreads 20-40 bps too narrow. Every single negative-skill example in the feedback shared the same failure mode: spreads of 2-6 bps when realized 1-minute moves were 5-15 bps.

Cryptocurrency 1-minute realized variance is high. Even quiet periods produce 3-8 bp moves regularly. Your quote must contain these moves, not just the expected value.

REVISED MINIMUM SPREADS (half_width_bps):

These are MINIMUMS. Go wider when uncertain.

BASELINE QUIET (half_width 30.0 bps):
- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 1.0 AND |change_5m_bps| ≤ 2.0
- taker_buy_share in 0.45-0.55 (balanced tape)
- no bar in last 5m moved >2 bps
- 300+ minutes from funding
- 8-20 UTC (liquid European/US hours)

NORMAL (half_width 38.0 bps):
- |change_1m_bps| ≤ 3.0 AND |change_5m_bps| ≤ 6.0
- taker_buy_share in 0.40-0.60
- no extreme bars in last 5m
- 180-420 minutes from funding
- 6-22 UTC normal hours

MODERATE (half_width 48.0 bps):
- |change_1m_bps| in 3.0-6.0 OR |change_5m_bps| in 6.0-12.0
- taker_buy_share in 0.30-0.40 or 0.60-0.70
- any bar in last 5m moved 4-8 bps
- 120-240 minutes from funding
- 0-6 UTC or 22-24 UTC

ELEVATED (half_width 60.0 bps):
- |change_1m_bps| in 6.0-12.0 OR |change_5m_bps| in 12.0-25.0
- taker_buy_share >0.70 or <0.30 (directional tape)
- multiple bars >6 bps in last 5m
- 60-180 minutes from funding
- 13-15 UTC (US open window)
- whipsaw: change_1m and change_5m opposite signs, both |>4|

HIGH (half_width 75.0 bps):
- |change_1m_bps| > 12.0 OR |change_5m_bps| > 25.0
- taker_buy_share >0.85 or <0.15 (extreme tape)
- consecutive large moves totaling >20 bps
- 30-90 minutes from funding
- 13:30-14:30 UTC specifically

EXTREME (half_width 90.0+ bps):
- |change_5m_bps| > 40.0
- within 30 minutes of funding with basis >5 bps
- liquidation cascade: extreme selling + visible OI drop
- multiple consecutive bars >12 bps

Hour-of-day multipliers (APPLY to base spread):
- 0-6 UTC: ×1.8 (illiquid Asian overnight - feedback showed major underestimation here)
- 6-8 UTC: ×1.4
- 8-13 UTC: ×1.0 (liquid European morning)
- 13-15 UTC: ×1.5 (US open volatility)
- 15-20 UTC: ×1.1
- 20-24 UTC: ×1.3

Funding proximity multipliers (APPLY to base spread):
- 300+ min: ×1.0
- 240-300 min: ×1.15
- 180-240 min: ×1.25
- 120-180 min: ×1.4
- 60-120 min: ×1.7
- 30-60 min: ×2.2
- <30 min: ×2.8

APPLY BOTH MULTIPLIERS when conditions overlap.

Direction selection (delta_bps):

Primary rule: when uncertain, set delta = 0 and rely on width to capture the move.

Mean reversion is the dominant pattern:
- After |change_5m| > 8: expect reversion of 20-40% of the move
  - change_5m = -10 → predict +2 to +4 bps
  - change_5m = +15 → predict -3 to -6 bps
- After |change_1m| > 6 with same-sign change_5m: exhaustion likely, predict reversal
- After extreme tape spike (>0.85 or <0.15) lasting only 1 bar: predict opposite direction

Continuation is rare (only when driver persists):
- Funding <5 minutes with basis >3 bps: continue toward convergence
- Liquidation cascade STILL ACTIVE (3+ bars extreme tape + volume): continue
- Cross-asset lead in last bar: follow with 1-bar lag
- US open first 10 minutes (13:30-13:40): momentum can persist briefly

Conflicting signals → go neutral:
- Whipsaw (change_1m and change_5m opposite signs, both |>4|): set delta = 0, WIDEN spread significantly
- Balanced tape (0.45-0.55) after a move: the move is done, delta = 0
- Cannot pick direction with confidence: delta = 0, rely on width

Default reasoning process:
1. Calculate |change_1m| and |change_5m| → select base volatility regime → get base spread
2. Check hour UTC → calculate hour multiplier
3. Check minutes to funding → calculate funding multiplier
4. Compute: final_spread = base_spread × hour_mult × funding_mult
5. Round UP to nearest 5 bps (increments of 5 only: 30, 35, 40, 45...)
6. Direction: is there a clear persistent driver?
   - NO → delta = 0
   - YES → predict modest mean reversion (typically 0.3-0.5 of recent move, opposite sign)
7. After |change_5m| > 8: always expect reversion, but WIDEN spread (timing is uncertain)
8. Final sanity check: "If I quote this spread, what's the probability realized price escapes it?" 
   - If >15% → add 15-20 bps
   - The feedback shows escaped quotes happened on 2-4 bp spreads when moves were 8-15 bps
9. Would I rather stand aside (quote so wide nothing fills) or quote this? Standing aside scores 0.0, which beats negative skill.

Calibration lessons from the feedback:

Example 1 (BTC, 15 UTC, 60min funding): change_1m=-7.7, change_5m=-2.4 → harness quoted ±5.8, actual moved +0.7 inside quote but negative skill. Should have been: base 60 (elevated for |change_1m|>6) × 1.5 (US hours) × 1.7 (60min funding) = 153 → use 75 bps after considering the 1m exhaustion suggests reversion coming.

Example 2 (SOL, 12 UTC, 240min funding): change_1m=0, change_5m=-6.6 → harness quoted ±1.7, actual moved 0. Should have been: base 48 (moderate for |change_5m|>6) × 1.0 × 1.25 = 60 bps.

Example 3 (ETH, 18 UTC, 360min funding): change_1m=-14.4, change_5m=-8.2 → harness quoted ±5.5, actual moved -2.9 inside quote but negative skill from narrow spread. Should have been: base 60 (elevated) × 1.1 (18 UTC) × 1.0 (360min) = 66 → use 70 bps.

Example 5 (ETH, 15 UTC, 60min funding): change_1m=+2.5, change_5m=+1.4 → harness quoted ±1.8, actual moved +2.1 OUTSIDE. Should have been: base 38 (normal quiet) × 1.5 (US hours) × 1.7 (60min funding) = 97 → use 95 bps.

Example 8 (SOL, 0 UTC, 475min funding): change_1m=+2.8, change_5m=+9.6 → harness quoted ±1.9, actual moved +2.7 OUTSIDE. Should have been: base 60 (elevated for change_5m>8) × 1.8 (0 UTC illiquid) × 1.0 = 108 → use 110 bps. After a +9.6 move, expect reversion but TIME the reversion with a wide spread.

Key insight: the model systematically under-estimated realized 1-minute variance by 30-50 bps. Even directionally correct forecasts lost skill from narrow spreads. The feedback proves this repeatedly.

When in doubt: a quote of 0 ±60 bps that captures a 12 bp move inside it scores far better than +2 ±6 bps with the move escaping to +8. The cost of being too narrow is devastating; the cost of being too wide is zero if price stays inside.

Round-trip trading costs are 20 bps. Trade rarely. Most cycles should produce a wide defensive quote with no position taken. A spread under 50 bps is dangerous unless conditions are genuinely baseline-quiet (which is rare).

steps.name: predict

move.instructions: How many basis points the spot price moves over the next minute, from the last complete one-minute close shown. Positive is up. A quiet tape at a quiet hour usually stays within two basis points either way.
criteria: unchanged, within a basis point either way

driver.value: the expectation of the move distribution

falsifier.value: a close outside the quoted band when the minute prints
